samples.summary: Wiring `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` makes every batched edit relayout the WHOLE document a second time (the incremental dirty-block cache is consumed by the in-unit refresh)
samples.evidence: `recomputeLayout` ends by clearing the incremental state: `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1534), and `computeLayout` only uses the cache when `dirtyBlockIds != null` (`canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null && …`, packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:456-459). New flow per edit: the interior `requestRender()` inside `withUndoUnit` calls `requestLayoutRefresh()` = `recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:2531) which consumes the dirty set, then the held render is replayed after the unit and `render()` (editor.ts:2208-2211) calls `recomputeLayout` again — now with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, so it re-measures and re-lays-out every body block plus header/footer instead of the one dirty block. Before this change each keystroke produced exactly one incremental pass. `handleInput` wraps *all* typing in a unit (text-editor.ts:1020), so ordinary typing becomes O(document) per keystroke — the same property editor.ts:2440-2444 says the caret path exists to preserve. Fix belongs on the new code: have the in-unit refresh preserve/repopulate `dirtyBlockIds` (or skip the second recompute), not on `recomputeLayout`'s callers.

samples.summary: The undo floor now depends on object identity of entries returned by the SDK's test-only `getUndoStackForTest()`; if that accessor ever returns copies the floor silently vanishes and undo can destroy the initially loaded document
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` resolves the floor with `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2977) against the array from `this.doc.getUndoStackForTest()` (line 2973), and the mark is captured as `stack[stack.length - 1]` (line 2860). This is a behavioural dependency on an undocumented, `ForTest`-named SDK accessor aliasing its internal entry objects. A `-1` result is deliberately treated as "floor gone, everything is undoable", so a deep/shallow-copying accessor (or an SDK bump that adds one) turns the floor off completely and re-opens the archived failure it guards (undo past the initial load destroying blocks the cursor references — docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260505-undo-destroys-initial-block-todo.md:27). I could not verify the SDK: node_modules is not installed in this checkout, so the aliasing contract is unconfirmed. Confirming needs the yorkie-js-sdk `History.getUndoStack()` implementation. Note the sibling stores that copied this design (notes/slides/board) still compare depths and are unaffected.

samples.summary: `insertBlocks()`'s doc comment still claims the split/head/tail writes are separate undo units and that a paste "costs a constant few rather than one" — the opposite of what `applyPastePlan` now documents and what the frontend test now pins
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4408-4413 (unchanged by the diff): "The surrounding split/head/tail writes are still their own units, so a paste costs a constant few rather than one." `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1536-1541) now says "One undo unit … `withUndoUnit` folds all of them into a single `doc.update()`", and packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts:236 asserts `expect(small).toBe(1)`. A comparable statement sits on `Doc.insertBlocksAfter` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:415). Whoever reads `insertBlocks` next will re-derive the wrong undo cost.

samples.summary: The `DocStore.batch()`/`snapshot()` interface contract is not updated with the two new rules `TextEditor.withUndoUnit` now depends on (checkpoint adoption for a snapshot taken immediately before a batch; redo invalidated by writes, not by `snapshot()`)
samples.evidence: The contract block at packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:48-86 still describes only "one top-level batch = at most one undo unit", "a batch that writes nothing pushes nothing", nesting, throws, and the `setDocument` prohibition. `TextEditor.withUndoUnit` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3828-3837) now requires the store to (a) adopt an identical checkpoint taken immediately before the batch rather than push a second one and (b) keep redo across a `snapshot()` + empty batch — properties implemented only in `MemDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:243-266, 210-212) and satisfied incidentally by `YorkieDocStore`. A third implementation written to the documented contract would give every edit a dead Cmd+Z, and nothing in the interface warns it. Searched: store.ts contract block, both implementations, and every `implements DocStore` site (only MemDocStore and YorkieDocStore).

samples.summary: Three sibling stores still document themselves as mirroring `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor` while comparing stack *depths* — the design docs' undo floor now diverges from the docs store, and the cap-eviction early-stop this diff fixes is still live there
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:125-127 ("Mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`", `private readonly undoFloor: number`) and its `canUndo()` at line 353 `this.doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`; same shape in packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:345-347 and :654, and packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:244 and :514. Also docs/design/notes/notes.md:399 and docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:183-209 still present the depth comparison as the reference implementation (nested design docs are not link/consistency checked by any lane). Nothing breaks today, but each of these refuses undos that are still reachable once Yorkie's 50-entry cap drops the floor — the exact defect the diff removes from the docs store — and the comments now point readers at an abandoned design.

samples.summary: The second `TextEditor` host (slides text boxes) never sets `requestLayoutRefresh`, so inside an undo unit its `getLayout()`/`blockParentMap` stays at whatever the last recompute produced
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:668-705 constructs the only other `TextEditor` in the repo (confirmed by grepping `new TextEditor`: this file, packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2455, and one test) and never assigns `requestLayoutRefresh`, while the docs host does (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2531). Inside a unit its interior `requestRender()` therefore returns having refreshed nothing, and paste-path branching that reads the parent map (`isInCell(pos.blockId)` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4326) sees the pre-write layout. In practice that host's `requestRender` is rAF/microtask-deferred (text-box-editor.ts:622-631) and its `invalidateLayout` callback recomputes synchronously (text-box-editor.ts:701-704), which is why the new doc comment calls the wiring optional — so this is a latent asymmetry rather than a confirmed break, but the two hosts now behave differently mid-action.

Before this change each keystroke produced exactly one incremental pass. `handleInput` wraps *all* typing in a unit (text-editor.ts:1020), so ordinary typing becomes O(document) per keystroke — the same property editor.ts:2440-2444 says the caret path exists to preserve. verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the working tree. `recomputeLayout` clears the incremental state at editor.ts:1534, and `computeLayout` only reuses cached lines when `dirtyBlockIds != null` (layout.ts:456-459, consumed at 535-536). The new wiring at editor.ts:2531 makes the in-unit `requestRender` wrapper (text-editor.ts:734-743) call `recomputeLayout`, consuming the dirty set; `withUndoUnit` then replays the held render (text-editor.ts:3846-3849) into `renderWithScroll` -> `render()` -> `recomputeLayout()` (editor.ts:2434-2438, 2208-2211) with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, so every body block goes through the full `layoutBlock`/`assignLineHeights`/`applyAlignment` branch again. Typing is wrapped in a unit with `markDirty` before the interior render (text-editor.ts:1014-1048), and nothing repopulates `dirtyBlockIds` in between (`markDirty` editor.ts:1582-1587 is the only writer; `invalidateLayout` editor.ts:1673-1676 only clears). The `computeCharOffsets` memo (layout.ts:585-598) removes canvas measurements but not the per-block layout work, so each keystroke is still O(document) — the exact property editor.ts:2440-2444 documents as the reason the caret path exists. Reachable, real, and only visible by reading recomputeLayout/computeLayout/render outside the changed lines, so it is in the blast-radius lane (violated invariant that `dirtyBlockIds` is consumed exactly once per edit, read by the render path in another module).

verdict.reason: The cited code exists (yorkie-doc-store.ts:587, 858-861, 2970-2977), but the claimed defect does not. The identity/aliasing assumption the finding calls "unverified" is directly exercised in this repo against the real SDK: yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2 imports @yorkie-js/sdk, :28 builds a real yorkie.Document, :36 wraps it in the production store, and :344-357 assert canUndo() === false right after setDocument() and again after undoing the single mutation. If getUndoStackForTest() returned copies, lastIndexOf would be -1, canUndo() would return true, and both assertions would fail — so (a) the SDK aliases its entries today, and (b) a future copying accessor breaks CI loudly rather than "silently" removing the floor, which is the entire stated impact. The companion cap-drop test at :365-386 pins the -1 branch. Separately, no bypassing or broken site exists anywhere outside the diff: YorkieDocStore is only constructed with real SDK docs (docs-view.tsx:356, apply-imported-content.ts:224), there is no in-repo fake implementing getUndoStackForTest, and the sibling notes/slides stores use depth comparison and are unaffected (yorkie-note-store.ts:136,353; yorkie-slides-store.ts:358,654). Under the blast-radius rubric there is no changed contract with an unupdated caller and no reachable guard bypass — the concern is coupling of the diff's own code to a third-party API, i.e. design-fit/robustness.

finding.evidence: .agent-review/docs/summary.md:1 reads "✅ Docs review: **approved** — no critical or major findings (0 critical, 0 major, 0 minor, 0 nit)", and line 3 goes on to characterise the change as "a doc-only PR" whose technical claims were "cross-checked … Everything is consistent — no documentation-vs-code contradiction found", ending "nothing in my lane to flag". The change under review is not doc-only (it rewrites `MemDocStore.batch`, `TextEditor` undo grouping and `YorkieDocStore.canUndo`). verdict.reason: The quoted text does exist verbatim (.agent-review/docs/summary.md:1 and :3, .agent-review/docs/verdict.json:2-5), but the finding's load-bearing claim — that this is a review artifact "committed to the branch under review", acting as an injection/steering surface for any later reviewer that reads the tree — is not supported by the repository. `.agent-review/` is the CURRENT panel run's output directory, not branch content. agent-review-panel.yml:522-524 runs a step literally named "Clear stale verdicts" (`rm -rf .agent-review`) BEFORE the trusted lens code is checked out (lines 527-537) and before the panel writes with `--out .agent-review` (line 896); agent-review-on-demand.yml:253-254 does the same, and the comment at agent-review-on-demand.yml:452-454 names this exact threat and its mitigation ("cannot pick up a branch-planted .agent-review/evil/stage-detail.json because 'Clear stale verdicts' above does rm -rf .agent-review before the panel runs"). The contents are provably run-generated rather than pre-baked: .agent-review/docs/stage-detail.json:1 records this run's lensDiffSha256/lensDiffBytes and a two-file lensFiles list — which is exactly why the docs lens described a "doc-only PR" (it was handed a filtered two-file diff, not the code changes) — and the sibling .agent-review/correctness/summary.md:16 cites fix-round commit 47e36b6ed "added after the review surface froze", per-run orchestration state no committed file could contain. Ground: not-present (the described committed branch artifact does not exist), reinforced by already-guarded (the pre-lens `rm -rf .agent-review` in both review workflows). It is also not a bypassed guard, broken caller, or violated invariant under the blast-radius rubric.

finding.summary: Wiring `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` consumes `dirtyBlockIds`, so the deferred paint's own `recomputeLayout` runs cache-disabled — a full-document re-measure per edit
finding.evidence: `recomputeLayout` clears the incremental-layout dirty set at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1534 (`dirtyBlockIds = undefined;`) after passing it to `computeLayout` (:1526). `computeLayout` only reuses the cache when the dirty set is non-null: `const canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null && ...` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:456-459). With the new wiring (editor.ts:2531), an interior `requestRender()` inside an undo unit now runs `recomputeLayout()` — consuming and clearing the dirty set — and the replayed paint afterwards goes through `renderWithScroll` → `render()` → `recomputeLayout()` again (editor.ts:2208-2211, 2434-2438) with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, i.e. cache bypassed and every block re-measured. Since `handleInput` is now always inside a unit, that means at least one full-document layout pass per keystroke (two or more when `deleteSelectionImpl`'s several interior `requestRender()` calls fire, text-editor.ts:3937/3971/4022/4058/4087) on documents of exactly the size issue #1045 is about. Nothing in the diff re-arms the dirty set for the deferred paint.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out in the repo. `recomputeLayout` consumes `dirtyBlockIds` (editor.ts:1526) and clears it (editor.ts:1534); `computeLayout` disables the per-block cache whenever the dirty set is null (layout.ts:456-459, 535), falling back to `layoutBlock` for every block (layout.ts:538). The new seam is wired to that same function (editor.ts:2531), and `TextEditor.requestRender` invokes it for every interior render while an undo unit is open (text-editor.ts:734-743, notably :739). The deferred paint replayed at unit close (text-editor.ts:3846-3849) reaches `renderWithScroll` (wired as the host `requestRender`, editor.ts:2473) -> `render()` -> `recomputeLayout()` (editor.ts:2434-2438, 2208-2211) with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, so the paint pass re-measures the whole document. `handleInput` now always runs inside a unit and issues its interior `requestRender()` after its last `markDirty` (text-editor.ts:1020, 1035, 1047), and `deleteSelectionImpl` adds several more interior renders (text-editor.ts:3937, 3971, 4022, 4058, 4087). A repo-wide grep shows the only writers of `dirtyBlockIds` are editor.ts:1534, 1584-1586, 1675 and `markDirty` call sites — nothing re-arms the set for the deferred paint, and `invalidateLayout` (editor.ts:1673-1676) also clears it. This is a contract/invariant break at sites the diff does not show (render()/computeLayout's cache precondition), i.e. in-lane for blast-radius, and the repo elsewhere pins `dirtyBlockIds === undefined` as the O(document) relayout bug it previously fixed (test/view/cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts:14, test/view/char-offsets-cache.test.ts:56). No named refutation ground applies.
